items.headline: Claude in Chrome Is Now Fully Released, and It Can Act on Its Own
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude in Chrome browser extension, which lets Claude see whatever page you're on and take actions like clicking links, filling out forms, and moving between tabs, is now generally available (out of beta) for paid Claude plans. New safety checks scan a page for hidden malicious instructions before Claude acts, so it can now do more without asking your approval for every single step.
items.why_it_matters: If you'd been holding off on Claude in Chrome because it was 'still in beta,' this is Anthropic's signal that it's ready for daily use. That matters for a solo business owner who wants an assistant that can actually click around a site and fill in a form for you, not just answer questions in a chat window.

items.headline: Federal Judge Rules the Pentagon's Blacklisting of Anthropic Was Illegal
items.summary: A U.S. federal judge ruled that the Department of Defense illegally blacklisted Anthropic as a "national security supply chain risk" after the company refused to let Claude be used for autonomous weapons or domestic mass surveillance. The judge called the government's justification "illegal and baseless" and said it violated Anthropic's First Amendment and due process rights.
items.why_it_matters: This doesn't change how you use Claude day to day, but it's a reassuring data point about the company behind a tool a lot of us build our workflow around: Anthropic held its ground on where it won't let Claude be used, and won in court.

items.headline: ChatGPT Can Now Juggle More Than One Gmail and Google Calendar Account
items.summary: OpenAI updated ChatGPT so you can connect a personal and a work Gmail, Google Calendar, or Google Contacts account at the same time in one conversation, instead of being limited to just one. ChatGPT can now pull information from whichever connected account is relevant, or check across all of them together, when you ask it something.
items.why_it_matters: If you run your business out of one inbox and keep a separate personal one, or juggle a couple of client accounts, this means you can finally ask ChatGPT to check your schedule or dig up an email without disconnecting and reconnecting accounts first.

items.headline: Google's New AI Model Turns Your Rambling Voice Notes Into Clean Text
items.summary: Google launched Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, a speech-to-text AI that can catch you correcting yourself mid-sentence ("let's meet Tuesday, no wait, Wednesday"), strip out "ums" and "ahs," and auto-format the result. It already powers Google's voice-typing keyboard feature and is coming soon to Chrome so you'll be able to dictate into any text box on the web.
items.why_it_matters: If you dictate emails, video scripts, or social captions instead of typing them, this should mean noticeably cleaner results with less cleanup afterward once it rolls out more broadly to the tools you already use.

items.headline: Runway Is Killing Its Unlimited Plan on September 1
items.summary: Runway, the popular AI video generation tool, is retiring its Unlimited subscription. Monthly subscribers automatically move to the new Max plan at the same $95/month price on September 1, while annual Unlimited subscribers can choose to switch to Max or get a refund for their remaining months.
items.why_it_matters: If you or someone in your circle pays for Runway's Unlimited plan, don't ignore this: Max works differently (9,500 monthly credits instead of unlimited generations), so it's worth checking your account now to understand how your usage will be affected before the switch happens automatically.

opportunity.action_note: If you're on Runway's Unlimited plan, log in this weekend before September 1 to see your new Max credit allotment, or request a refund if you're on an annual plan and want out instead.

items.headline: Meta Takes Out Newspaper Ads Pressuring TikTok and YouTube on Teen Safety
items.summary: Days after agreeing to a multibillion-dollar settlement over how Facebook and Instagram treated younger users, Meta ran full-page newspaper ads publicly pressuring TikTok and YouTube to adopt similar teen-safety measures, like usage time limits.
items.why_it_matters: This is a sign more platforms may soon face similar pressure, restrictions, or settlements over how they treat younger users. Worth watching if your content or business reaches a teen audience on any of these platforms.
